title: I2C Two Sensors in a Maze
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Learning MicroPython
description: A robot drives a maze while the CPU polls an MPU-6050 accelerometer and then a gyroscope (same chip, 0x68) or an HMC5883L compass (0x1E) over one I2C bus. Shows raw bytes, charts, a bus timeline of reads taking turns, and the effect of the read rate.

educational.topic: Reading two I2C sensors on one bus
learningObjectives: Explain why two I2C sensors on one bus are read one after another, not at the same instant
Describe what an accelerometer and a gyroscope or compass each measure about a moving robot
Explain why a slow read rate can miss quick changes

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Exploration with a sample-rate slider and a sensor selector
keyQuestions: Can two I2C devices send data at the same moment?
Which sensor reacts when the robot speeds up, and which when it turns?
What do you lose when the CPU reads less often?
commonMisconceptions: Sensors on a bus transmit at the same time (the single controller serializes the reads)
The accelerometer and gyroscope are separate chips (they share one MPU-6050 and one address)
assessmentOpportunities: Student explains the alternating blocks on the bus timeline
Student matches chart features to robot motions
